chapter: Chicago and the New Orleans bands
title: Meeting Keppard and the Stroll
summary: He met Freddie Keppard at the Asia Cafe on the Stroll, where the entertainment places were, and played mostly theaters.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: When did you first meet him or hear him?

Well, I met Freddie at, well, I was playing at the Owl Theater, and at nights I would go down on the Strobe, we call it, around the Asia Cafe, and you could meet mostly anyone there. That was a hangout, the Chinese restaurant.
Uh, what did I say that was, Brian? Asia Cafe. Asia Cafe. Yeah, Asia Cafe at 35th and State. Asia, A-S-I-E. Oh, yeah.

Asia. Asia. Chinese restaurant. And I met Freddie there. And then, at that time you had, that was a stroll, we had the stroll, and there was a place of entertainment, two and three in a block. And you just walked from 31st to 35th, and you go in mostly the, any of the places of entertainment, they had a band there.
Trevor Compton was telling me about the E-Light number one, number two, and the Deluxe, and Dreamland were all along there. Yeah. Did you play those places too, or mostly just the theaters? Theaters.
Theaters. Mm-hmm. And after, after our places I also would play there. Yeah.

Yeah. Uh, while we're thinking of Keppard, I did want to ask a good deal about that, about him, because you made the only record that his name was ever on the label, Freddie Keppard, the Stockyard and the Salty Dog. Yes. You were on that date. And then the other record was made about the same time, the one under your name.
